en: The Sūtra on the Story of King Māndhātṛ, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakara of the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, while the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling in seclusion and solitude, this thought occurred to him:
"Even up to the point of being stained by and attached to sensual desire, one stores it all away; yet there is no satiety in sensual desire."
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, went to where the Blessed One was, and upon arrival, prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet and sat down to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda withdrew for a moment, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Just now, when I went to my place of meditation, this thought arose: [the mind] is stained by and attached to sensual desires, never reaching satiety."
At that time, the World-Honored One said to Ānanda: "So it is, so it is! Ānanda!"
Even unto the point of being stained by craving and attachment for hoarding and storing, there is truly no satiety. Why is this so, Ānanda?

Long ago, in the distant past, there was a great king named Mūrdhaja, a true Dharma-king who governed and transformed the people without violence or cruelty, and who was endowed with the seven treasures.

What are called the seven treasures are: the wheel treasure, the elephant treasure, the dark-blue horse treasure, the jewel treasure, the woman treasure, the householder treasure, and the military commander treasure; these are known as the seven treasures.

He also has a thousand sons, valiant, fierce, and robust, their countenances radiant and capable of repelling all enemies; like the rivers and great oceans of this world, he governs and transforms by means of the Dharma, without employing the sword or staff.
At that time, Ānanda!
King Māndhātṛ then had this thought:
"I have heard that in the past, people were extremely long-lived, intelligent, and wise."
He then spoke these words:
"Indeed, I possess this Jambudvīpa, which is endowed with power, majesty, and supernormal faculties; its crops are lush and abundant, and its population is dense."
Then the king had this thought:
"I wish to cause the seven treasures to rain down within my palace.
At that time, Ānanda!
After King Mūrdhaja had formed this thought, it rained the seven treasures for seven days.
At that time, on another occasion, King Mūrdhaja again had this thought:
"I have heard that in the past there were people of former times whose lifespans were extremely long and who were intelligent and wise."
"I have heard that there is Fuyudai, where the divine powers are sovereign, the grain is lush and abundant, and the population is dense.
I wish to go there to govern and transform them.
At that time, Ānanda!
As soon as King Mūrdhaja had formed this thought, he vanished from Jambudvīpa and appeared in Pūrvavideha, together with his fourfold army.

At that time, the beings of Pūrvavideha saw King Mūrdhaja approaching from afar; surrounded by a great multitude, they each took silver bowls filled with broken gold, or golden bowls filled with broken silver, and went to where King Mūrdhaja was. Having arrived, they addressed King Mūrdhaja: "Welcome!"
"Great King!

This is the realm of Pūrvavideha belonging to the Great King, where supernormal powers are sovereign, the grain is lush and abundant, and the population is dense. We pray that the Great King will govern and transform this land; we are all subjects under your command."
"At that time, Ānanda!
King Mūrdhaja ruled and transformed [the realm] for countless hundreds of thousands of years.
At that time, Ānanda!"
At another time, King Māndhātṛ thought to himself: "I possess the continent of Jambudvīpa;
my desires are fulfilled at will through my supernormal powers, the grain is lush and abundant, and the population is dense."

I have already rained down the seven treasures upon my palace for as long as seven days; now, furthermore, within the realm of Pūrvavideha, there is sovereign supernormal power, the crops are lush and abundant, and the population is dense.
I have heard that in the past, there were wise and sagacious elders who spoke thus:
"In the land of Aparagoyānī, supernormal powers are sovereign, the grain is lush and abundant, and the population is dense."
Then the king thought to himself:
"I wish to go to the realm of Aparagoyānī to lead and transform its people.
At that time, Ānanda!
Having formed this thought, King Mūrdhaja vanished from Pūrvavideha and proceeded to the realm of Aparagoyānī together with his fourfold army.

At that time, the people of Aparagoyānī saw King Mūrdhaja from afar; each took a silver bowl filled with fragments of gold, or a golden bowl filled with fragments of silver, and went to present them as offerings to King Mūrdhaja.
Having arrived, he addressed King Mūrdhaja, saying: "Welcome,
Great King!"

"This is the realm of King Aparagoyānī; its grain is lush and abundant, and its population is dense and flourishing. We pray only that Your Majesty will lead and transform the people of this realm of Aparagoyānī; we are all subjects under Your Majesty's governance."
"At that time, Ānanda!
King Māndhātṛ governed and transformed the people of Aparagoyānī for countless hundreds of thousands of years and countless tens of thousands of years.
At that time, Ānanda!"
At another time, King Māndhātṛ again had this thought:
"I possess the land of Jambudvīpa, where grain and food are abundant and the population is dense; for seven days, the seven treasures rained down upon my palace;
I also possess the realm of Pūrvavideha, where I have mastery over supernormal powers, grain and food are lush and plentiful, and the population is dense."
"There is also the realm of Aparagoyānī, where one possesses mastery of supernormal powers and reaches a land of dense population.
At that time, King Mūrdhaja thought to himself:
"I have heard that in the past, there were wise and intelligent people of old who spoke these words:"
“There is the realm of Uttarakuru, where the power of the divine feet is sovereign and the population is dense.

In that land, all the people have no sense of belonging; they act with autonomy as they desire and their lifespans are exceedingly long. When their lives there end, they are all reborn in the heavens. They eat naturally grown non-glutinous rice and wear garments of karpāsa cotton.”
At that time, King Mūrdhaja thought to himself:
"I shall rule and transform that realm.
As soon as he had this thought, Ānanda!
King Mūrdhagata vanished from Aparagodānīya and proceeded to the realm of Uttarakuru, accompanied by his fourfold army.

At that time, King Mūrdhagata saw from afar that the ground of that country was entirely level and uniformly deep blue; having seen this color, he addressed his ministers and the people: "O you all!..."
"Do you see that the ground is level, even, and deep blue-black in color?
He replied, "It is so."
"O Great King!
If you wish to know, this is the *karpāsa* (cotton) tree.
Those people all wear *karpāsa* garments; you, too, should wear *karpāsa* garments."
At that time, King Māndhātṛ again saw that the earth was a pure white color; having seen it, he spoke again to his ministers:
"Do you all see that this ground is white?"
He replied, "It is so.

[The Buddha asked,] "This is naturally grown non-glutinous rice, without husks and without stalks; it requires neither beating with sticks nor winnowing. Its fragrance extends one hundred yojanas with the wind and fifty yojanas against the wind—exceedingly fragrant and exquisite."
"The people of that land eat this non-glutinous rice; you virtuous ones should also eat this non-glutinous rice.
At that time, King Mūrdhaja saw from afar that the ground was level and uniform, entirely the color of deep blue. Having seen it, he addressed his ministers and the people, saying:
"Do you see this deep blue color?"
He replied, “It is so,
Great King!”
"This is four-finger-width soft grass, as exceedingly soft as peacock feathers, each curling to the right and indistinguishable from their own bodies.
The people of Uttarakuru all sit upon this grass; you, too, should sit upon this grass."
At that time, King Mahāsudarśana saw from afar the city walls, watchtowers, and battlements; having seen them, he addressed his ministers and the people, saying: "O you all!..."
"Do you see that this ground is level and even, and that the watchtowers and battlements are intact? He replied, "It is so."
"Great King!
This is the dwelling of the people.

At that time, the inhabitants of Uttarakuru saw King Mūrdhaja approaching from afar; each took a golden bowl filled with silver grain and a silver bowl filled with golden grain, and addressed King Mūrdhaja, saying:
"Welcome, Great King!
This is the realm of Uttarakuru, where supernatural powers are sovereign, the grain is lush and abundant, and the population is flourishing."
"May Your Majesty rule and transform the people of Uttarakuru, and we shall likewise obey your royal instructions.
At that time, Ānanda,
King Mūrdhaja ruled and transformed the people of Uttarakuru for countless hundreds and thousands of years.
At another time, King Māndhātṛ again had this thought:

"The realm over which I rule includes the continent of Jambudvīpa; it is vast, sovereign in its spiritual power, and teeming with people. There, I caused the seven treasures to rain down upon my palace for as long as seven days.
I also possess the continent of Pūrvavideha, which is likewise vast, sovereign in its spiritual power, and teeming with people."
I also possess the continent of Aparagoyānī, where my supernormal powers are sovereign and the population is flourishing;
I also possess the continent of Uttarakuru, where my supernormal powers are sovereign and the population is flourishing.
I have heard that in the past there were wise and intelligent people who spoke thus:
"There is a Heaven of the Thirty-three with an exceedingly long lifespan and handsome countenances; therein dwells a deva named Śakra Devānām Indra."

"I shall now go to those Trāyastriṃśa gods and there receive the five states: divine lifespan, divine appearance, divine pleasure, divine majesty, and divine sovereignty; I now wish to go to the Trāyastriṃśa heaven."
"At that time, Ānanda!
Having formed this thought, King Mūrdhaja vanished from Uttarakuru and proceeded to dwell in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, together with his fourfold army, arriving at the Sudharma Hall."
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra saw King Mūrdhaja approaching from afar; having seen him, he spoke to King Mūrdhaja, saying:
"Welcome, Great King!"
"You may take this seat.

Then, Ānanda, King Mūrdhaja sat down upon the seat and shared it with Śakra Devānām Indra. These two kings sat together without distinction; their countenances and features were exactly equal and no different, except for the blinking of their eyes.
At another time, King Mūrdhaja again thought to himself:
"I possess the continent of Jambudvīpa, where my supernormal powers are sovereign and the population is dense; for seven days, I have caused the rain of the seven treasures to fall upon my palace.
I also possess the realm of Pūrvavideha, where my supernormal powers are sovereign and the population is dense."
I also possess the continent of Aparagoyānī, where I travel with mastery of supernormal power to its densely populated regions;

I also possess the continent of Uttarakuru, where I travel with mastery of supernormal power to its densely populated regions; and I dwell here in this Heaven of the Thirty-three, long-lived and remaining for a great duration.
At that time, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven assembled in the Sudharmā Hall and each sat down in their respective order.
Then, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven thought to themselves:

"This King Mūrdhaja is the ruler of Jambudvīpa; he governs by means of the Dharma, possesses the seven treasures, is surrounded by a thousand sons, and is the most honored and supreme among the four borders. He governs the people through the Dharma without the use of weapons or staffs."
At that time, Ānanda!

Śakra Devānām Indra offered half of his seat to King Mūrdhaja to sit upon; the two sat together with no difference in their radiance, and their complexions and features were entirely identical, differing only in the blinking of their eyes.
"At that time, Ānanda!
King Mūrdhaja amused himself with those five sensual pleasures for countless hundreds of thousands of years and countless tens of thousands of years, never reaching satiety."
At that time, Ānanda!
At another time, King Mūrdhaja again had this thought:

"The realm over which I rule includes the land of Jambudvīpa, where my supernatural power extends and the population is flourishing; for seven days, the seven treasures have rained down upon my palace."
There is also the realm of Aparagoyānī, which I reach by means of my supernormal power, where the population is flourishing;
I also have the realm of Aparagoyānī, which I reach by means of my supernormal power, where the population is flourishing;
I also have the realm of Uttarakuru, which I reach by means of my supernormal power, where the population is flourishing.
Furthermore, there are these Trāyastriṃśa gods whose lifespans are long and whose complexions are radiant.
There is this Sudharmā Hall for their righteous discourse, complete with four gardens.
What are the four?
There are four gardens: the Cūṭaka Garden, the Ratnavicitra Garden, the Karkaśa Garden, and the Miśrakāvana Garden.

In these gardens grow the pārijātaka tree and the kovidāra tree, both of which are lush and flourishing; their fragrance extends one hundred yojanas with the wind and fifty yojanas against the wind. This is the place where the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven enjoy themselves, delighting in the five sensual pleasures for four months.

This is the Hall of Dharma Discourse for the Virtuous; it is entirely made of blue lapis lazuli. This is the place where the Lord of Devas sits, surrounded by a hundred tiers all fashioned from the seven precious gems. Each tier has seven hundred pavilions, each pavilion has forty-nine jade maidens, and each jade maiden has forty-nine attendants; all are under the command of Śakra Devānām Indra.
"At that time, Ānanda!
King Māndhātṛ again had this thought:
'I shall now displace Śakra Devānām Indra and govern and transform the various devas here in the Heaven of the Thirty-three.'"
"At that time, Ānanda!
As soon as King Mūrdhaja gave rise to this thought, he and his fourfold army fell from the seat of Śakra Devānām Indra down to Jambudvīpa."

Having lost his supernormal power of the bases of mastery, his entire body was in pain, just as when a person is about to die: the wheel-treasure vanished, the elephant-treasure passed away, the horse-treasure also came to its end, the jewel-treasure no longer appeared, the woman-treasure passed away, and the householder-treasure and the military-commander-treasure passed away.
At that time, Ānanda!
King Māndhātṛ’s five kinds of kinsmen all gathered together and went to where King Māndhātṛ was, addressing him, saying:
"After the Great King has passed away, there may be those who question us: [what did you do?]"
"When Great King Mandhātu is on the verge of passing away, what final instructions will he leave behind?
How shall we answer him? At that time, King Mandhātu replied:
"If, after my life has ended, there should be one who asks:
'What were King Māndhātṛ's final instructions when he was on the verge of death?
you should answer him thus:"

"Virtuous ones, you should know that King Mahāsammata, who ruled over the four continents, went to the Heaven of the Thirty-three; there, he met no end to his craving for the five objects of sensual pleasure and subsequently passed away."
“Ānanda! If you wish to know, who was that King Mūrdhaja at that time?
Do not view it in such a way.”
For what reason?
Ānanda, the king at that time was none other than myself.
By this means, Ānanda, you should know that even regarding the five desires there is no satiety; being stained by and attached to desire, one accumulates and stores it, for there is no end to desire.
"What is called 'sufficiency' is to reach the path of the noble sages; only then is one sufficient.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Not by means of wealth or occupation, But by awakening to the knowledge of detachment from desire, One attains sufficiency."
Pleasure is little and suffering is much; this is not what the wise do.
Even amidst the five desires, they ultimately find no delight in them.
When craving is exhausted, one attains true happiness; such are the disciples of the Buddha.
Bound by the craving for food, one will ultimately enter hell;
though one originally desires security, life is tormented by suffering.
All phenomena are entirely impermanent; that which is born must inevitably decay.
"All that is born must come to an end; that cessation is the supreme bliss.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Story of King Mūrdhaja Spoken by the Buddha
